clue.text: Description of unfinished cake, perhaps, spotted

blocks.note: first meaning, split as two words: a cake still lacking its topping
second meaning: seen, observed

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a cake left only half decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: read the answer as two words and it describes a cake still waiting for its icing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spotted is to have been seen or observed, which the past tense of this verb also means.

clue.text: Beginner can’t get a grip, it seems?

blocks.note: a flat refusal or negative, as in no can do
a vice is the clamp on a workbench whose job is to grip things

explanation.surface: A learner keeps fumbling and cannot keep a firm grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a grip' sounds like advice to calm down; the question mark warns that it is meant literally, about a workbench clamp (American spelling: vise).
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a newcomer or learner, someone just starting out at a skill or trade.

clue.text: Fastener caught up on leg, unfortunately

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading letters from bottom to top
something that goes unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters end up in a bad order

blocks.note: caught, as in got hold of
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fastener has snagged on someone's leg, unluckily.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the reversed piece sits on top of the second, so 'on' is the charade's positional link.
explanation.definitionFit: A toggle is a short bar-shaped button pushed through a loop, as on a duffel coat, so it fastens things.

clue.text: Tidied up of course, in describing “spruce” say?

indicators.note: tidying up rearranges things into a new order, so the letters are reorganised

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it also joins the fodder to the definition

explanation.surface: Of course 'spruce' means tidied up, a word-lover remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' as an adjective means neat, which chimes with 'tidied up'; here it is the evergreen tree, and the quotation marks hint it is being treated as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce is a cone-bearing evergreen tree, so the adjective for cone-bearing trees describes it.

clue.text: Object bird found in centre of Madrid

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, so only those are kept
something found in another sits inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: the middle two of six letters
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: An object such as a bird turns up in the middle of the Spanish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun for a thing but is the verb meaning to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance, a slightly formal synonym of object as a verb.

clue.text: Place for patient with bad plague

blocks.note: a hospital patient lies in one
wicked, bad

explanation.surface: A hospital ward is set aside for someone suffering from a terrible plague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plague' reads as a disease noun to fit the hospital picture, but it is the verb meaning to torment.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil someone is to trouble or harass them persistently, just as to plague them is.

clue.text: China supports offensive game

indicators.note: in a down entry, what supports sits beneath, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: unpleasant, offensive
Minton is a famous make of English porcelain

explanation.surface: The Chinese state backs an aggressive sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: China with a capital letter points to the country, but it is porcelain; Minton is a Staffordshire pottery brand. In a down clue the supporting word goes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net, so it is a game.

clue.text: See a lover, fruity thing

blocks.note: first meaning: to go out romantically with someone
second meaning: the sweet brown fruit of a palm tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' hints at something racy to fit the lover, but it simply means a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to court someone romantically, and the noun names the sticky fruit of the palm.

clue.text: Group of religious followers changes around Old Testament

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: alters, changes
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A sect alters its scriptures around the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Votaries are devoted worshippers bound by vows, so collectively they are religious adherents.

clue.text: Lethargic, having lost record?

blocks.note: a written record, a list
the suffix meaning without

explanation.surface: Someone feels sluggish after losing a record, perhaps a vinyl disc.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the answer means without a list; the question mark signals that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless describes someone lacking energy or enthusiasm, a close synonym of sluggish and lethargic.

clue.text: Careful eater, say, in vehicle

indicators.note: a piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a van is a vehicle
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A fussy eater sits in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it qualifies the definition but supplies EG, the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan avoids all animal products, so they must be choosy and watchful about food.

clue.text: Adopting change, more than one friend thinks deeply

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in and make one's own, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: plural of mate, a friend
to edit is to change

explanation.surface: A group of friends ponders hard before accepting change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' is a verb here, giving EDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect or contemplate at length, focusing the mind in serious thought.

clue.text: State where African oil spilled

indicators.note: spilled liquid splashes everywhere, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A country where oil from Africa has leaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' could be a verb or a country, but it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: California is one of the fifty United States, on the Pacific coast of America.

clue.text: Exam welcomed by professor, always

indicators.note: what is welcomed is taken inside, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A professor always welcomes an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma between the two words is ignored; the letters run straight across the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, often a viva in which a candidate answers questions in person.

clue.text: Lawful position where one may be taken for a ride?

definitions.text: where one may be taken for a ride

blocks.note: just, lawful
a position held, as in stand your ground

explanation.surface: A legal standpoint where someone might be swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken for a ride' usually means cheated; the question mark signals the literal sense of going on a roller coaster or carousel.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is an outdoor site with carousels and roller coasters, so visitors are literally given rides.

clue.text: More than one problem arises with banter that’s out of order

indicators.note: anything out of order is not in its proper sequence, so the letters need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out after some inappropriate joking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arises' reads as the verb of the sentence but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainteasers are puzzles that test the mind, so several of them are a set of problems to solve.

clue.text: At first not out of it? I join forces

blocks.note: the opposite of out, as a batter still at the crease
taken as written
taken as written
to ally is to join forces

explanation.surface: Someone first left out of things decides to team up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the sentence oddly; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Initially means in the beginning or to start with, an adverb meaning the same as at first.

clue.text: Underwater creature, one fish in net hauled up

indicators.note: placing something in another means it sits inside it
in a down entry, hauling upward makes the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a parr is a young salmon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea creature and a fish are caught in a net and pulled aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the one and the fish inside the net, then read the whole result upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a freshwater turtle that spends much of its life swimming beneath the surface.

clue.text: Great thinker thus requires a load of beer!

blocks.note: so means thus
beer delivered in boxes, a load of crates

explanation.surface: A great mind needs plenty of beer to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark marks the comic image of a philosopher fuelled by ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the classical Athenian philosopher, teacher of Plato, widely regarded as a great mind.

clue.text: Developing rebel missing at the front

indicators.note: something missing at the front has lost its opening letter

blocks.note: a rebel against the established order

explanation.surface: An insurgent in training is absent from the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the R from the start of the rebel word.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolutionary describes gradual change and growth over time, so it fits an adjective meaning developing.

clue.text: Spanish dish bound to be served up with half of lamb

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read from bottom to top
half a word keeps just part of its letters, here the opening pair

blocks.note: a bound is a jump
the first half of the word, two of its four letters

explanation.surface: A Spanish dish is sure to come with some lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as 'certain to be', but bound is the noun for a jump and 'to be' is padding in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is the Valencian rice dish cooked with saffron, seafood or meat in a wide shallow pan.

clue.text: Sounding like iron, for example, steel

indicators.note: a word that sounds like another is spoken the same but spelt differently

blocks.note: iron is one example of the material class

explanation.surface: Iron rings like steel when struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel' looks like another metal, matching the iron, but it means inner toughness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is courage and resolve, the quality called steel in phrases like nerves of steel.

clue.text: Red not often seen

blocks.note: first meaning: meat cooked lightly so it stays red inside
second meaning: uncommon

explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour or a communist, but it describes steak barely cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes underdone meat still red in the middle, and also anything scarce or uncommon.

clue.text: Two possibilities served with notice, roughly

blocks.note: to serve food is to give it out
the word that links two alternatives
to take is to notice, as in take note or take in

explanation.surface: Two options were presented along with a rough warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces do not appear in clue order: the alternatives word sits between the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase give or take means approximately, allowing a little either way, as in an hour give or take.

clue.text: Land in foxhole

blocks.note: first meaning: ground, soil
second meaning: a fox's underground den

explanation.walkthrough: 'Land in foxhole' suggests a soldier diving for cover; a fox's burrow has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ground or soil, and also the burrow where a fox lives.

clue.text: Reportedly single person

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by speech, so a sound is meant

blocks.note: sole means single or only

explanation.surface: Word has it someone is unattached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single person' reads as an unmarried individual, but single gives the sound and person is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soul is used to mean an individual, as in not a soul in sight or a kind old soul.

clue.text: Poor work adding chicken to pan

blocks.note: a cooking pot
a boiler is an older chicken fit only for boiling

explanation.surface: A cook does a bad job by tossing chicken into the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: The pan comes first even though the chicken is mentioned first: chicken is added to pan. A boiler is a tough old bird for the stockpot.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a hastily produced novel or artwork made just to earn money, of low quality.

clue.text: Dark element encapsulating minimum of levity

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose in a capsule, so one piece wraps another
the least possible amount of a word is a single letter, its first

blocks.note: a component or element
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A gloomy part of something contains very little humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' suggests chemistry but here means a component, a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit describes a place without lighting, so it is dark, with no lamp or fire burning.

clue.text: Inhalation’s ending with a rush – snuff taken like that

indicators.note: an ending is the last part, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter, ignoring the apostrophe-s
taken as written
a sally is a sudden rush forward, as from a besieged fort

explanation.surface: A sharp sniff ends with a rush as the snuff goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter belongs to the word 'Inhalation', the possessive tells you whose ending it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Snuff is powdered tobacco sniffed up into the nostrils, so it is taken through the nose.

clue.text: Awfully dry heat – add water

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In fierce arid heat, you need to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' reads as 'very', intensifying the heat, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To hydrate is to supply something with moisture, combining it with or soaking it in liquid.
